title: Biaxial Basal Tone and Passive Testing of the Murine Reproductive System Using a Pressure Myograph
protocol: Determine the estrous cycle by visual assessment.
Perform experiment at the estrus stage.
Euthanize mice for basal tone testing via guillotine.
Euthanize mice tested only under passive conditions using CO2 inhalation.
Dissect within 30 minutes to minimize cell apoptosis.
Set up an absorbent pad on the workstation.
Fill a Petri dish and syringe with 4 °C Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS).
Use a wipe for adipose tissue disposal.
Place the mouse ventral side up and tape the paws and tail.
Turn the microscope lights on.
Set out micro-scissors, scissors, two pairs of straight tweezers, and two pairs of curved tweezers.
Lift the skin around the abdomen using angled tweezers and scissors.
Make an incision at the base of the abdomen above the pubic bone without puncturing the abdominal muscle wall.
Continue cutting superiorly towards the rib cage through the abdominal muscles.
Remove superficial fat by pulling lightly with curved tweezers and micro-scissors.
Place all removed fat and tissue on the wipe.
Identify both uterine horns and the pubic bone.
Place closed scissors between the vaginal wall and the pubic bone.
Carefully cut the middle of the pubic bone (pubic symphysis).
Place curved tweezers on both ends of the cut pubic bone.
Pull both cut ends laterally to allow better access to reproductive organs.
Remove the bladder and urethra from the vaginal wall using straight tweezers and micro-scissors.
Hold the bladder with straight tweezers to create tension.
Use blunt dissection techniques to separate the surrounding tissue from the vagina.
Cut the base of the dissected bladder and urethra and remove it from the body cavity.
Identify the cervix from the vagina based on differences in geometry and stiffness.
Mark 3 mm dots along the reproductive organs starting below the ovaries using ink and calipers.
Place dots inferiorly to reach the cervix, then continue down to the vagina introitus.
Use a center cervix dot as the starting point for marking a path down to the vaginal introitus.
Allow the ink to dry completely before proceeding.
Separate the reproductive organs from surrounding adipose tissue, connective tissue, and the colon.
Clean the vagina as close to the vaginal introitus as possible using appropriate techniques.
Cut around the vaginal introitus with scissors.
Cut the uterine horns immediately inferior to the ovaries.
Place the dissected reproductive organs in a Petri dish filled with 4 °C HBSS.
Measure the space between dots using calipers.
Record the measurements for each distance into a spreadsheet.
Set the wipe that contains the discarded tissue on the abdominal region with the excess tissue facing the inside of the mouse.
Soak the wipe in 4 °C HBSS.
Wrap the mouse and excess tissue in foil.
Place the wrapped mouse in a freezer safe bag to be stored at -20°C.
Determine the proper cannula size for the organ type.
Use a cannula with a diameter of 3.75 mm and riveted for the vagina in typical C57BL6J mice.
Use one cannula that is 3.75 mm for the vaginal end and another cannula that is 0.75 mm smooth for the uterine end for the cervix.
Mount the cervical side of the organ on the force transducer portion of the cannulation device.
Mount the opposite end of the organ (vaginal or uterine) on the micrometer portion of the device.
Tighten both ends with sutures.
Place 2 sutures in a "X" fashion between the 2nd and 3rd rivets of the cannula for the vagina.
Use 3 horizontal sutures on the uterine end and 4 sutures on the external os when cannulating the cervix.
Ensure that the maximum length is no more than 7 mm between the sutures.
Power on the testing system.
Fill the reservoir bottle with 200 mL of HBSS.
Turn the heat to “on” and allow the HBSS to heat up.
Turn on the microscope.
Open the computer program.
Ensure that the image of the cannulated organ, pressure interface, flow meter readings, and the sequencer function tool are visible.
Stretch the organ so that the wall is not in tension.
For the vagina, observe the grooves on the vaginal wall.
For the cervix, cut immediately below the ink dots located above and below the central cervix mark.
Measure the length from suture to suture with calipers.
Increase the pressure from 0 to 10 mmHg in increments of 1 mmHg.
Determine the pressure at which the organ is no longer collapsed as the largest jump in the outer diameter at a given pressure.
Record the pressure and outer diameter when the organ is not collapsed.
Zero the force after recording the first point wherein the organ is not collapsed.
Calculate the estimated in vivo stretch by dividing the length measured in vivo by the length measured post-explant.
Set the pressure to 0 mmHg, the length to the estimated in vivo length, and the gradient to 1.5 mmHg/s.
Run a sequence that takes the pressure from 0 mmHg to the in vivo pressure plus unloaded, holds for 30 seconds, and returns to 0 mmHg with another hold period of 30 seconds.
Repeat this cycle for a total of 5 cycles.
Press Stop in the computer program after completing the cycles and save the file.
Adjust the organ to be at the estimated in vivo length while at the unloaded pressure.
Press Start to begin assessing pressure vs force values from the unloaded pressure to the maximum pressure.
Press the Stop button when assessment is complete and save the file.
Set the pressure to 0 mmHg, the length to the experimental in vivo length, and the gradient of 1.5 mmHg/s for pressure-diameter pre-conditioning.
Run a sequence that increases the pressure from 0 mmHg to the maximum pressure + UP, holds at this pressure for 30 seconds, returns to 0 mmHg with an additional 30 second hold period.
Repeat this cycle for a total of 5 cycles.
Press the Stop button in the program interface after completing the cycles and save the file.
Enter 1/3 max pressure + UP for both the inlet and outlet pressure.
Adjust the organ to -2% of the in vivo length and press Start.
Adjust the length to +2% in vivo length then back down to -2% at 10 µm/s.
Repeat axial extension for a total of 5 cycles.
Press Stop in the computer program and save the file.
Set both the inlet and outlet pressure at 1/3 of the maximum pressure + UP.
Equilibrate the organ for 10 minutes.
Slowly bring both pressures back down to 0 mmHg with the gradient set as 1.5 mmHg/s.
Set the organ to the in vivo length and the pressure to the unloaded pressure.
Decrease the axial length towards the estimated unloaded length at a rate of 10 µm/s until there is minimal change in the force.
Record the unloaded length, outer diameter, and the force value before zeroing the force.
Use the general imaging abdominal package to visualize organs in the testing device.
Adjust the cannula to a height that is the maximum distance from the bottom of the pressure myograph metal basin while ensuring tissue remains fully submerged.
Stabilize the transducer in a vertical position using a custom 3D printed holder.
Identify the cannula near the force transducer and adjust the microscope stage to image along the length of the tissue.
Track the middle region along the length of the tissue throughout the testing process.
Review the image “Cine store” loop consisting of B-mode frames and identify the frame with the largest outer diameter.
Press Start and adjust the organ so that it is -2% of the in vivo length.
Set the pressure to 0 mmHg and gradient to 1.5 mmHg/s.
Increase the pressure from 0 mmHg to the maximum pressure.
Bring the pressure back down to 0 mmHg with a 20 second hold period.
Repeat this for 5 cycles.
Press Start and adjust the organ so that it is at the in vivo length.
Set the pressure to 0 mmHg and gradient to 1.5 mmHg/s.
Increase the pressure from 0 mmHg to the maximum pressure.
Bring the pressure back down to 0 mmHg with a 20 second hold period.
Repeat this for 5 cycles.
Adjust the organ so that it is +2% of the in vivo length.
Set the pressure to 0 mmHg and gradient to 1.5 mmHg/s.
Increase the pressure from 0 mmHg to the maximum pressure.
Bring the pressure back down to 0 mmHg with a 20 second hold period.
Repeat this for 5 cycles.
Set the pressure to the unloaded pressure and the organ to -2% of the in vivo length.
Stretch the organ to +2% of the in vivo length at a rate of 10 µm/s.
Return the organ to -2% of the in vivo length at a rate of 10 µm/s.
Repeat for a total of 3 cycles.
Set the pressure to 1/3 of the maximum pressure + UP and adjust the organ to -2% the in vivo length.
Stretch the organ to +2% the in vivo length and back to -2% the in vivo length at a rate of 10 µm/s for 3 cycles.
Press Stop and save the data after completing the stretch cycle.
Set the pressure to 2/3 of the maximum pressure + UP and adjust the organ to -2% the in vivo length.
Stretch the organ to +2% the in vivo length and back to -2% the in vivo length at a rate of 10 µm/s for 3 cycles.
Press Stop and save the data after completing the stretch cycle.
Set the pressure to maximum pressure + UP and adjust the organ to -2% the in vivo length.
Stretch the organ to +2% the in vivo length and back to -2% the in vivo length at a rate of 10 µm/s for 3 cycles.
Save the data after completing the stretch cycle.
Remove KRB testing media from the tissue.
Wash the tissue with calcium-free KRB solution.
Replace the media with calcium-free KRB solution supplemented with 2 mM EGTA.
Incubate the tissue in the new solution for 30 minutes.
Remove the calcium-free KRB solution after incubation.
Replace the media with fresh calcium-free KRB solution.
Stretch the organ so the wall is not in tension.
Measure the cannulated organ from suture to suture and record as unloaded length.
Increase pressure from 0 to 10 mmHg in increments of 1 mmHg.
Determine the pressure at which the organ is not in tension.
Zero the force and record this pressure, outer diameter.
Calculate estimated in vivo stretch by dividing the length measured in vivo by post-explant length.
Set pressure set to 0 mmHg, length as estimated in vivo length, gradient to 1.5 mmHg/s.
Begin running a sequence that takes pressure from 0 mmHg to maximum and back to 0 mmHg.
Repeat this process through 5 cycles with a 30 second hold time.
Adjust the organ to the in vivo length.
Manually enter the unloaded pressure for both pressures into the computer program.
Press Start and set the gradient to 2 mmHg, and the pressure to 1/3 of the maximum.
Stretch the organ up to +2% and back down to -2% stretch at 10 µm/s.
Repeat the stretching cycle for a total of 5 times.
Press Stop after completing the force-length preconditioning cycles.
Find and plot force values at -2%, the in vivo length, and +2% of the in vivo length.
Take forces at evenly spaced pressures ranging from 0 mmHg to the maximum pressure.
Determine the experimental in vivo stretch value that exhibits a relatively flat line over a range of pressures.
Repeat the pressure diameter and axial preconditioning steps at the new in vivo length.
Set the inlet and outlet pressure to the unloaded pressure with the organ at the determined in vivo length.
Let the organ re-equilibrate for 15 minutes.
Slowly bring the inlet and outlet pressure back down to 0 mmHg after 15 minutes.
Bring the organ to the unloaded length and re-estimate the unloaded length.
Record the unloaded length and outer diameter while the pressure is 0 mmHg, the unloaded pressure, and 1/3 the maximum pressure.
Zero the force at the unloaded pressure.
The diameter at the unloaded pressure is the in vivo diameter.
Re-estimate the unloaded length due to small plastic deformations observed previously.
Perform ultrasound B-mode imaging at the unloaded length and pressure.
With the organ at -2% of the experimentally determined in vivo length and the pressure at 0 mmHg, press Start.
Increase the pressure from 0 mmHg to the maximum pressure and back to 0 mmHg.
Hold the 2-0 mmHg step for 20 seconds.
Repeat the pressure-diameter testing process for a total of 5 times.
Press the Stop button in the interface after completing the tests, then save the file.
Perform ultrasound B-mode imaging at the experimental in vivo length and +2% of the experimental in vivo length.
Set the pressure to nominal pressure and adjust the organ to -2% of the in vivo length for force-length testing.
Stretch the organ up to +2% of the in vivo length and back to -2% of the in vivo length at a rate of 10 µm/s.
Repeat the stretching process for a total of 3 times.
Perform force-length testing at 1/3 max pressure, 2/3 max pressure, and at the maximum pressure.
Calculate the unloaded thickness from ultrasound images B-mode image.
Using imaging software, draw a line to denote the penetration depth.
Set the scale to the length of the line for accurate measurements.
Using a computer software, trace and measure the inner diameter of the organ.
Measure the outer diameter of the organ.
Draw a line between the measured inner and outer diameters.
Draw 25 transmural lines for measurement.
Average all data points from the measurements.
Repeat the process for a total of three times.
Ensure that the pressure is set to 0 mmHg and turned off.
Close the main inlet and outlet for both three-way valves.
Aspirate any remaining fluid from the basin of the cannulation device.
Remove the organ from the stage and fill the reservoir bottle with deionized water.
Rinse the cannula with water using a syringe.
Connect tubing to bypass the cannula.
Turn on the pressure and flow, setting the inlet pressure to 200 mmHg.
Set the outlet pressure to 0 mmHg and gradient to 10 mmHg/s.
Let the flow run for five minutes.
Allow the system to continue running until the reservoir bottle is empty and lines are dry.
For pressure diameter testing, collect data from where the pressure starts increasing from its minimum value until reaching the maximum.
For force-length testing, collect data starting just below the peak in force until the force stops decreasing.
Open the data file for each pressure-diameter test.
Select the mean pressure tab.
Navigate to the loading region of the last curve, from 0 mmHg to the maximum pressure.
Drop the data into a spreadsheet.
Select the same region on the outer diameter and drop the data into the same document.
Select the inlet pressure data from the same region and place it in the spreadsheet.
Select the outlet pressure data from the same region and place it in the spreadsheet.
Select the force data from the same region and place it in the spreadsheet.
Select the temperature data from the same region and place it in the spreadsheet.
Select the pH data from the same region and place it in the spreadsheet.
Select the flow data from the same region and place it in the spreadsheet.
Open the data file for each Force-length test.
Navigate to the loading region of the curve, from -2% to +2%.
Drag and drop the data into a spreadsheet.
Select the inlet pressure data from the same region and place it in the same spreadsheet.
Select the outlet pressure data from the same region and place it in the same spreadsheet.
Select the force data from the same region and place it in the same spreadsheet.
Select the temperature data from the same region and place it in the same spreadsheet.
Select the pH data from the same region and place it in the same spreadsheet.
Subtract the UP from all pressure values.
Average the pressure-diameter data every 1 mmHg (i.e., 0+/- 0.5, 1+/-0.5, 2+/- 0.5).
Calculate the unloaded volume of the organ using Equation 1.
Measure the unloaded outer radius by microscope and calculate the radius.
Measure the unloaded length with calipers from suture to suture.
Detect the unloaded thickness from ultrasound images.
Use the unloaded volume, deformed outer radius, and length to determine the deformed inner radius.
Calculate each stress using Equations 3, 4, and 5, where P is defined as the intraluminal pressure and Ft is the force measured by the transducer.
Plot the pressure-diameter relationship.
Plot the force-pressure relationship.
Plot the circumferential stress-circumferential stretch relationship.
Calculate axial stress using Equation 7.
Calculate circumferential stress using Equation 6.
Calculate compliance near the physiological pressure range and at the in vivo stretch.
Determine the lower pressure bound as 1 standard deviation below the mean measured pressure.
Determine the upper pressure bound as 1 standard deviation above the mean measured pressure.
Identify the circumferential stress that corresponds to the lower pressure bound.
Identify the circumferential stress that corresponds to the upper pressure bound.
Fit a linear line to the circumferential stress-circumferential stretch curve within the identified stress range at the in vivo length.
Calculate the slope of the fitted line to quantify material stiffness.
